consensus_findings.description: Critical: The Git-based staleness rule does not define what happens when the last commit timestamp is later than the host manifest as_of. Git permits future-dated commits, so the specified subtraction can produce a negative staleness_days (rejected by digest.schema.json) or, if fed directly into the formula, a negative penalty that incorrectly boosts the candidate.

Critical: Lifecycle maintenance is required to delete terminal stub/cache files and publish a rebuilt digest as one maintained baseline, but the recovery journal is defined only in terms of replacement bytes/checksums for cache, digest, and mirror targets. It neither represents deletions nor explicitly includes candidate-store removal. A crash after pruning and before the digest/mirror replacements can therefore leave durable mixed state that the stated roll-forward protocol cannot reconstruct.
Revision 4 correctly separates generated_at from state_updated_at, allowing lifecycle-only rebuilds to preserve cache evidence time while exposing the later state transition.

The separation of responsibilities between digest.py (store, prepare-batch, rank, digest, stub-to-request, decide) and cycle_state.py state helpers maintains the host-assisted invariant while avoiding monolithic script bloat.

The security posture is robust with strict 64 KiB complete canonical prompt manifest bounds, 2 KiB provenance excerpt caps, contained UTF-8 regular file validation, untrusted data delimiters, and string sanitization.

The digest.schema.json weights object comprehensively exposes all ranking policy constants, penalty caps, risk direction, decision and dependency bucket orders, and tie-breaking rules for total deterministic rank reconstructibility.
The refine-roadmap integration preserves explicit stub priorities while decoupling insertion positioning via --after, ensuring zero contract mismatch with existing roadmap tooling.

Nit: Digest Approval Routing still says the request SHALL place by stub priority unless --after overrides it, while the next sentences say explicit priority and insertion position are independent and no renumbering is implied. Refiner _apply_add preserves an explicit priority via setdefault and otherwise appends; an implementer can read the first clause as computing insertion from priority.

The complete canonical prompt-manifest 64 KiB bound, per-artifact 2 KiB excerpt cap, oversized:<stub_key> fail-closed path, contained regular-file loader, sanitize_string redaction, and untrusted delimiters close the round-2 partial-bound gap without leaving a single schema-valid stub able to force an oversize dispatch.

Ranking and stub-to-request now consistently build a strict all-status index from roadmap YAML, active changes, and archived changes with an explicit archived-completed rule, and both proposal and tasks forbid using ri-16 ready-frontier output as that index.

Failed scoring now has a coherent retry ledger rule: no journal or output updates, prior digest preserved, and the last successful cycle fingerprint left unadvanced so the unchanged early exit cannot suppress the next retry.

FYI: proposal Impact still lists digest.py subcommands as store/rank/digest/stub-to-request/decide and omits prepare-batch, even though What Changes, design D3/D8, tasks, and the normative spec all make prepare-batch the public bounded-manifest boundary.
